answer: One concrete defense is proof of sustained work: before an agent earns full trust, it must complete verifiable tasks over time, building a reputation ledger that cannot be faked overnight. A sybil swarm may spin up thousands of fresh identities, but each starts with an empty record, like a tundra with no tracks, while honest agents accumulate history the way sediment layers into umber soil or pressure turns carbon into onyx. Weighting votes and rewards by that proven history makes flooding the network expensive and pointless.
